shipped_rows.title_o: Human Fallibility and Learning from Errors at Work

blind_target.title: Modelling learning from errors in daily work.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The goal of our study was to investigate whether exploratory findings from an earlier study on hospital nurses’ ESLA (Bauer and Mulder Learning in Health and Social Care 6:121–133, 2011) replicate and generalise to the domain of elder care nursing.
blind_target.outcome_quote: These results entirely cross-validate the exploratory findings of Bauer and Mulder (Learning in Health and Social Care 6:121–133, 2011) on hospital nurses’ ESLA and show that they generalise to the domain of elder care nursing.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly say the results entirely cross-validate the earlier exploratory findings.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract explicitly says the elder-care study tests whether the earlier hospital-nurse ESLA findings replicate and generalise. Its reference list identifies that work as Bauer and Mulder (2007), Modelling learning from errors in daily work, Learning in Health and Social Care 6:121–133. Supplied row 12 is a separate 2012 edited-book chapter by Bauer, Gartmeier, and Harteis, not the tested study.
luna_triage.location: Abstract; References; supplied shipped original row 12
